• ArchitecturalDecision — "get_relevant_context topic search: search_records (BM25 over label + description) replaces search_classes (label-only)"
  hasDescription: Commit caa6e387e6 (Merge search-records-integration). src/graph/mod.rs relevant_context(): entity_index.search_classes(t, &class_iris, &state.store, &data_graphs, moose::LABEL_PREDICATES, limit) replaced by entity_index.search_records(t, &class_iris, &state.store, &data_graphs, &text_fields, limit). text_fields = [(moose::RDFS_LABEL, 2.0_f32), (state.capture.description.as_str(), 1.0_f32)] — rdfs:label weighted 2× because every record carries it as its title; description weighted 1×. Searching rdfs:label rather than hasTitle ensures label-only records (no hasTitle) are still found and the title text isn't double-counted. BM25 is raw/corpus-relative — results are ranked and top-k selected rather than filtered by an absolute score. List-all path (no topic → list_instances via SPARQL) is unchanged. Tool remains purely symbolic: no LLM on the retrieval path.
  hasAuthor: James Adam <jcadam@startmail.com>
  hasLifecycleStatus: accepted
  isMotivatedBy: https://moosedev.dev/kg/Constraint/49d02d6e-b322-4584-9ce1-7f3c777ff055

  hasTitle: get_relevant_context topic search: search_records (BM25 over label + description) replaces search_classes (label-only)
  hasTimestamp: 2026-06-18T18:46:37Z
  rationale: entity_index.search_classes() with LABEL_PREDICATES matched only rdfs:label tokens — too narrow. A topic appearing only in a record's description would be missed entirely. Commit caa6e387e6 switches to entity_index.search_records() with BM25 weighted text fields (rdfs:label × 2.0, hasDescription × 1.0), covering both the primary label and the richer description content. The symbolic (no-LLM) constraint is preserved; only the matching surface expands.

• Lesson — "Recall-first means list-all: a topic-scoped empty result is not an empty graph"
  hasDescription: Commit 2145d71c95 (tasks/lessons.md). During the M4 bootstrap-skill dry-run, `get_relevant_context` was called with a specific topic, returned "No recorded knowledge relevant to …", and the agent concluded the graph was empty — then recorded decisions that already existed, creating duplicates. Rule: the recall-first step must be a list-all call (`get_relevant_context` with no `topic` parameter). A topic-scoped call returns only records whose embeddings align to that topic; it can silently miss related records that were captured under different framing. List-all is the only safe dedup check before recording. Apply at the start of every capture session and every temporal-bootstrap episode.
  hasAuthor: James Adam <jcadam@startmail.com>
  hasLifecycleStatus: accepted
  learnedFrom: https://moosedev.dev/kg/ArchitecturalDecision/122d4bd2-0c7e-4a72-8faa-227285e157ae
  hasTitle: Recall-first means list-all: a topic-scoped empty result is not an empty graph
  hasTimestamp: 2026-06-18T06:48:06Z

• ArchitecturalDecision — "get_relevant_context: BM25 search_records replaces entity-index absolute floor for noise rejection"
  hasDescription: Commit caa6e387e6 (Merge search-records-integration). src/graph/mod.rs: TOPIC_RELEVANCE_FLOOR constant deleted; .filter(|h| h.score >= TOPIC_RELEVANCE_FLOOR) removed from the topic-hit pipeline. Replaced by text_fields = [(RDFS_LABEL, 2.0), (state.capture.description, 1.0)] passed to entity_index.search_records(). BM25 scores are corpus-relative — results ranked top-k, no absolute threshold. Records sharing no query term are excluded by search_records itself, preserving invariant #6 (be correct, don't sound correct) without a fragile constant. tests/context.rs: noise-rejection test updated from "transport tuning methodology" (single incidental token overlap) to "kubernetes helm rollout" (genuinely zero shared terms), verifying BM25 exclusion rather than the old score floor. Comment updated: "rank and take top-k rather than applying an absolute floor; records sharing no query term are excluded by search_records, preserving the honest empty state."
  hasAuthor: James Adam <jcadam@startmail.com>
  hasLifecycleStatus: accepted
  isMotivatedBy: https://moosedev.dev/kg/Constraint/49d02d6e-b322-4584-9ce1-7f3c777ff055
  hasRationale: https://moosedev.dev/kg/Rationale/89c6a1a5-cd5f-44e6-a375-fd689e6539c6
  supersedes: https://moosedev.dev/kg/ArchitecturalDecision/03d8d242-c154-4b55-8b3b-781289fbcb6c
  hasTitle: get_relevant_context: BM25 search_records replaces entity-index absolute floor for noise rejection
  hasTimestamp: 2026-06-18T18:46:37Z
  rationale: TOPIC_RELEVANCE_FLOOR = 0.45 (absolute score threshold calibrated to entity-index scoring) is removed in commit caa6e387e6. BM25 over rdfs:label (weight 2.0) + hasDescription (weight 1.0) via search_records excludes zero-match records intrinsically, making the constant unnecessary. The floor was fragile: calibrated to one scoring scale and brittle across search-method changes. BM25 corpus-relative ranking + top-k provides stronger, more portable noise rejection without an arbitrary cutoff, while preserving the honest empty-state invariant (#6).
  https://moosedev.dev/kg/ArchitecturalDecision/19e2082a-10a5-4683-92a9-b7c53bff7a5d

• Constraint — "Relational expansion in get_relevant_context must be bounded: budgeted reach, not neighborhood dump"
  hasDescription: Commit 5dc4a3ba00 (src/graph/mod.rs, EXPAND_FROM_TOP/EXPAND_MAX_HOPS/EXPAND_MAX constants). Relational expansion in get_relevant_context is a budgeted reach to the few linked records that complete an answer — specifically the lexically-distant neighbor that BM25 alone misses — without dumping the full neighborhood. Concretely: expansion seeds from only the top-N BM25 hits (EXPAND_FROM_TOP=3), walks at most EXPAND_MAX_HOPS=2 hops outward, and appends at most EXPAND_MAX=5 total linked records. Context efficiency is the whole point of get_relevant_context: returning the entire reachable neighborhood would negate the retrieval tool's purpose of surfacing the most relevant records without overwhelming the caller's context window. Expansion is skipped entirely for list-all calls and when MOOSEDEV_EXPAND_HOPS=0.
  hasAuthor: James Adam <jcadam@startmail.com>

• ArchitecturalDecision — "Benchmark oracle mode: harness-side retrieval isolates knowledge-value from fetch-willingness"
  hasDescription: Commit 29cac60c28 (`bench/run.py`). A `mode="oracle"` parameter on `run_cell()` causes the harness to retrieve relevant knowledge and prepend it verbatim to the prompt, without giving the agent a live memory tool. This isolates two confounds: H8 (fetch-willingness — whether the agent chooses to call the memory tool) and knowledge-value (whether the knowledge itself helps). If oracle does not beat B0, the captured knowledge has no value; if live-tool < oracle, the gap is fetch-willingness alone.

Implementation: `oracle_context()` calls `get_relevant_context` for B2 (current-only, symbolic BM25); `freetext_oracle_context()` runs BM25 over the exported chunk file for B1 arms (currency-blind — superseded chunks are retrievable, same as what a B1-rag agent would get). Topic is `task["memory_topic"] or task["prompt"]` — a focused subject phrase so the retrieval signal is unambiguous.

Oracle asymmetry is intentional: the B2−B1 oracle delta isolates B2's currency-awareness (the agent acting on lifecycle status) rather than information withholding (B1 oracle would also retrieve superseded chunks, so if B2 oracle correctly ignores a superseded record and B1 oracle uses it, that gap is earned).

• Constraint — "Symbolic layer is primary: LLM is a sensor, not the controller"
  linkedVia: isMotivatedBy
  hasDescription: Design Invariant #1 from CLAUDE.md (initial commit 455628e081). The LLM is a sensor, not the controller. Whenever possible, prefer deterministic symbolic mechanisms (alignment, typed knowledge capture, session graph, focus stack, validation) over relying on the LLM to reason or remember correctly. The strength of MOOSEDev comes from the symbolic layer, not from making the LLM do more work. This is the primary guiding constraint on all tool and pipeline design.

• ArchitecturalDecision — "MOOSEDev: neurosymbolic MCP server to combat comprehension debt"
  linkedVia: constrains
  hasDescription: MOOSEDev is designed as a neurosymbolic MCP server whose core purpose is to combat comprehension debt — the gradual loss of understanding of why a codebase is structured the way it is. It serves as an early example of a domain-specific, epistemically grounded AI application. Built on top of the closed-source MOOSE neurosymbolic engine; MOOSEDev itself is open source. Rationale: push back against LLMs that optimize for sounding correct rather than being correct, by emphasizing symbolic reasoning, structured typed knowledge, auditability, and a living project knowledge graph. Established in CLAUDE.md (initial commit 455628e081).

item.text:
Currently, `get_relevant_context` uses symbolic `entity_index.search_records()` BM25 retrieval over record text fields: `rdfs:label` weighted `2.0` and `hasDescription` weighted `1.0`, returning ranked top-k current records with no absolute score floor; zero term-overlap records are excluded by the search itself.

It then may append a bounded relational expansion from the top BM25 hits: top 3 seeds, up to 2 hops, max 5 linked records, skipped for list-all calls or when expansion is disabled. Based on recorded entries “get_relevant_context topic search: search_records (BM25 over label + description) replaces search_classes (label-only)” and “Relational expansion in get_relevant_context must be bounded: budgeted reach, not neighborhood dump.”
